title.value: Exploiting Syntactic Structure for Better Language Modeling: A Syntactic Distance Approach
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the top of the research paper.
title.quote: Exploiting Syntactic Structure for Better Language Modeling: A Syntactic Distance Approach

analysis.description: This paper investigates incorporating syntactic structure into neural language models using a multi-task objective that predicts words and parse trees. The model improves language modeling performance by utilizing syntactic distances. The Ordered-Neuron LSTM (ON-LSTM) is used as the baseline model. The paper introduces the PTB-Concat dataset for evaluation, which is an enhanced version of the Penn Treebank dataset with syntactic information added back.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments using datasets like the Penn Treebank and provides empirical results, such as lower perplexity in language modeling due to incorporating syntactic structures.
type.quote: Experimental results on the Penn Treebank and Chinese Treebank datasets show that when ground truth parse trees are provided as additional training signals, the model is able to achieve lower perplexity and induce trees with better quality.

name.justification: The paper focuses on language modeling, which is a key area within Natural Language Processing (NLP).
name.quote: It is commonly believed that knowledge of syntactic structure should improve language modeling.

name.justification: The research primarily aims to enhance language modeling by integrating syntactic information, evident from the multi-task objective of predicting words and parse trees.
name.quote: However, effectively and computation-ally efficiently incorporating syntactic structure into neural language models has been a challenging topic.

name.justification: The Ordered-Neuron LSTM (ON-LSTM) is specifically mentioned as the baseline model for the experiments conducted in the paper.
name.quote: We choose the Ordered-Neuron LSTM (ON-LSTM) (Shen et al., 2018) as our baseline model, which gives the best results among distance-based models.
